contributions.statement: Do not let an orchestrating model choose the file paths and tools it grants to subagents; enforce per-role allowlists deterministically, because every evaluated manager over-granted (workspace-permission precision under 50%, 0.48-5.78 forbidden accesses per subagent).
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Finding 1, Table 3-4. Audit downgrades to weak: WPP's numerator is set by what the fixed Gemma worker reads, so the metric partly measures the worker, and there is one run per model on 41 synthetic non-SE scenarios. No enforcement layer is tested.

contributions.statement: Do not pick a manager model from an aggregate leaderboard score: ten models sat in a 9.9-point band while their orchestration behaviour (forbidden accesses, delegation style) differed more than 10x.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Finding 3, Fig. 3, Table 4; single run, so ranks inside the band are not separable, which is the point but also limits it.
relative_to: report behaviour metrics alongside pass rate (2607.22585)

reason: The over-granting observation motivates deterministic permission scoping, but it rests on a metric partly controlled by the worker, one run, and non-SE tasks; least privilege itself is already known. Keep as a hypothesis only.
